title: Boiler Feedwater Tank

introduction.definition: A boiler feedwater tank stores condensate returns and treated make-up water for the boiler feed pumps. Keeping it hot (often ~85–90 °C via a steam sparger) reduces dissolved oxygen and improves boiler efficiency.
applications: Before a deaerator in larger plants
introduction.summary: A boiler feedwater tank collects condensate returns and treated make-up water and holds a reserve for the boiler feed pumps. Keeping it hot (steam sparger) drives off oxygen and reduces corrosion and chemical dosing.

foundation: Set on a level foundation designed for operating, hydro-test and wind/seismic loads; grout base plates; anchor bolts per drawing.
alignment: Check verticality (vertical vessels) or level and slope (horizontal); one saddle bolted, the other slotted for thermal expansion.
piping: Connect nozzles without forcing — check allowable nozzle loads; support piping independently.
Fit the required pressure relief device and isolation as per code.
commissioning: Hydro/pneumatic test per code; inspect internals before closing; purge and leak test; commission instruments and relief valves.

lubrication: No lubrication — static equipment (lubricate valve stems and manway hinges only).

causes: Water too hot for available NPSH

video_tutorials.title: Boiler Feedwater Tank — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Boiler Feedwater Tank.
A boiler feedwater tank stores condensate returns and treated make-up water for the boiler feed pumps.
Keeping it hot (often ~85–90 °C via a steam sparger) reduces dissolved oxygen and improves boiler efficiency.
Typical applications include small/medium industrial boiler houses; before a deaerator in larger plants; condensate recovery systems.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Boiler Feedwater Tank.
Check level and temperature.
Check sparger and level gauge.
Internal inspection/coating.
Watch for pump cavitation: noise. Common cause: water too hot for available npsh.
Watch for corrosion: rust, leaks. Common cause: oxygen, low ph.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
